reasons: Composio removed its managed Twitter credentials in February 2026. Until you add your own X app's credentials to a custom auth config, the Twitter toolkit does not work at all.
X bills every API call to the developer account that owns the app, from prepaid credits. Your users' reads and posts are paid for from your credit balance, so the app has to be yours.

Several Composio Twitter tools (search, post lookup by IDs, usage) call X with an app-only Bearer Token that you paste into the auth config, and it must come from the same X app as your OAuth Client ID.

verdict.summary: No review: create an app, buy prepaid credits and any X user can connect the same day. The barriers are cost and terms: every read and post is billed (a post with a link costs $0.20), self-serve access is meant for a limited number of users, and beyond that X requires a negotiated Enterprise contract.

timeToTesting.label: 30-60 min, plus a card payment for credits

timeToProduction.label: Same day on pay-per-use. Enterprise, if X asks you to move to it: no published timeline

verdict.mainBlocker: Money and terms, not review: per-call billing from prepaid credits, X's rule that self-serve access only covers apps with a limited number of end-users, and API restrictions on what an agent may do (no programmatic follows or likes, replies only when summoned).

stages.name: Create the developer account and app
limits: The app's credentials (keys, secret, Bearer Token) are shown only once. Regenerating them invalidates the old ones.
Up to 10 callback URLs per app, matched exactly, including trailing slashes.

steps.title: Sign up in the X Developer Console
steps.detail: Go to console.x.com and sign in with the X account that should own the app. Use a company-controlled account, not a personal one: the app, its credits and its billing all belong to this account. Accept the Developer Agreement and Policy and describe how you will use the API. There is no approval queue for this step in X's current docs.
steps.humanReason: Requires signing in to an X account and accepting X's legal terms on behalf of your company.

preparedValues.label: Use case description (draft, edit to match your product)
preparedValues.value: Our product is an AI assistant that lets each user connect their own X account with OAuth 2.0 and, at that user's request, read their timeline, mentions and bookmarks and publish posts they approve. We do not use X content to train models, and we do not automate follows, likes or unsolicited replies.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: From the console dashboard, create a new app with a name, description and use case. Name it after your product. Save the API Key and Secret and the Bearer Token immediately: Composio needs the Bearer Token for its app-only tools, and the console does not show it again.
steps.humanReason: Inside your signed-in developer console; the credentials should pass only from the console to Composio.

steps.title: Set up OAuth 2.0 in User authentication settings
steps.detail: Open the app's User authentication settings and turn on OAuth 2.0. Choose Web App (or Automated App / Bot): both are confidential clients and get a Client Secret, which Composio needs. Native App and Single Page App are public clients and get no secret. Set permissions to read and write (add Direct Messages only if you use DM tools). Paste Composio's redirect URI as the callback URL. Copy it from your Composio auth config, not from Composio's older Twitter guide, which still shows a /api/v1/ path that Composio's own knowledge base calls legacy. Fill in the website URL with your product's site.

preparedValues.label: Type of app
preparedValues.value: Web App, Automated App or Bot (confidential client)

preparedValues.label: Callback URI / Redirect URL
preparedValues.value: Copy from Composio: Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > Twitter > OAuth2

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
steps.detail: Open Keys and Tokens and copy the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret. Treat the secret like a password: it goes into Composio and nowhere else.
steps.humanReason: The secret should only pass from your console to Composio.

stages.name: Buy credits and enrol in billing
limits: No free tier for new developers. Every read and write is charged from prepaid credits.
If the balance hits zero (it can go slightly negative), API requests are blocked until you add credits.
Pay-per-use accounts are capped at 3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle.

steps.title: Add a card and buy credits
steps.detail: In the console, add a payment method and buy credits. X requires a verified phone number to buy credits. As of October 2026, a new account's first card and first purchase earn $20 in free credits, and the first successful auto-recharge is matched up to $50. These free credits expire after 3 months and are still rolling out.
steps.humanReason: A payment and a phone verification on your company's account.

steps.title: Set a spending limit and auto-recharge
steps.detail: Set a spending limit per billing cycle so a looping agent cannot run up a bill: when the limit is reached, requests are blocked until the next cycle. Turn on auto-recharge if you want the connection to keep working when the balance runs low. Auto-recharge fires at most once per 5 minutes, so set the recharge amount high enough to cover a burst.
steps.humanReason: A spending decision for your company.

preparedValues.label: Spending limit for testing
preparedValues.value: Estimate: $10-25 per billing cycle is enough to test reads and a few posts

steps.title: Check the app is attached to a project enrolled in pay-per-use
steps.detail: If writes fail with a 403 'Client Forbidden' body containing registration_url and required_enrollment, or Composio shows client-not-enrolled or 'App not linked to project', the app is not attached to a project that is enrolled in pay-per-use billing. Attach it in the console and retry.

stages.name: Connect it in Composio and test
limits: Access tokens last 2 hours. Without offline.access there is no refresh token and the connection dies after 2 hours.
Each test call costs credits, for example $0.005 per post read and $0.015 per post created.

steps.title: Create the Twitter auth config in Composio
steps.detail: Create a Twitter auth config, toggle on your own developer credentials and enter the Client ID, Client Secret and Bearer Token from the same X app. Composio pre-fills scopes; remove those your agent does not use, and keep offline.access. Copy the auth config ID (it starts with ac_) into your secret manager.

preparedValues.label: Minimum scopes to read and post
Add for bookmarks, lists, DMs (only if used)
preparedValues.value: bookmark.read bookmark.write list.read list.write dm.read dm.write

steps.title: Connect your own X account and run one tool
steps.detail: Start a connection, approve X's consent screen, and run one cheap read (for example, look up your own user) and one post. If app-only tools such as search return 401 while user tools work, the Bearer Token is from a different app or your plan does not include that endpoint.
steps.humanReason: You approve the consent screen with your own X account.

stages.name: Open it to your users

duration.label: Same day: no review or publishing switch

limits: Self-serve access is for apps with 'a limited number of end-users'. X does not define the number; beyond it, X's terms require an Enterprise plan.
POST /2/tweets: 100 per 15 minutes per user, 10,000 per 24 hours per app, shared by all your users.
Replies only when the original author mentioned or quoted the replying account. Follows, likes and quote posts are not available on self-serve access.
X's terms forbid using X content to train or fine-tune a foundation or frontier model.

steps.title: Budget per user before launch
steps.detail: Every user's activity is billed to your credits. Posts with a URL cost $0.20 each, plain posts $0.015, post reads $0.005 and user reads $0.010. The cheaper $0.001 'Owned Reads' price only applies when the authenticated user is the owner of the developer app, so it does not cover your end users' own data. Rate limits are counted separately from billing: posting is capped at 100 per 15 minutes per user and 10,000 per 24 hours for the whole app.

steps.title: Remove tools X no longer allows on self-serve
steps.detail: Since April 20, 2026, following, likes and quote posts through the API are off for all self-serve accounts, so Composio tools such as TWITTER_FOLLOW_USER will fail. Since February 23, 2026, programmatic replies only work when the original author mentioned or quoted the replying account. Post analytics need Enterprise. Disable these tools in your agent so it does not retry them.

steps.title: Follow X's automation rules
steps.detail: Get each user's explicit consent before your agent sends automated replies or DMs, never do bulk actions, and label any bot account as automated. Apps that break the rules can be suspended; X notifies by email and appeals go through the Platform Help Form.

steps.title: Apply for Enterprise if you outgrow self-serve
steps.detail: If your user base or read volume goes beyond what self-serve covers (3 million post reads a month, or more than 'a limited number of end-users'), apply through X's Enterprise interest form. Pricing is negotiated; X publishes none, and third-party guides cite entry prices of about $42,000-50,000 a month. X can also review your usage on its own, suspend access and require an Enterprise application.
steps.humanReason: A commercial negotiation and contract for your company.

requirements.title: A card, prepaid credits and a verified phone number
requirements.detail: There is no free tier for new developers. Credits are bought upfront and deducted per call. Legacy Basic and Pro subscriptions are being moved to pay-per-use during 2026, so there is no fixed monthly tier to pick.

requirements.title: Stay within self-serve scope, or move to Enterprise
requirements.detail: X's pay-per-use agreement limits self-serve to hobbyists, prototyping, early-stage integrations and apps with a limited number of end-users. Beyond that you must apply for Enterprise.

requirements.title: offline.access for long-lived connections
requirements.detail: Without it, X issues no refresh token and the access token expires after 2 hours.

requirements.title: No model training on X content
requirements.detail: The agreement forbids using the X API or X content to fine-tune or train a foundation or frontier model. Keep X data out of any training pipeline.

requirements.title: Automation rules for write actions
requirements.detail: Explicit consent before automated replies or DMs, no bulk actions, and bot accounts must say they are bots.

blockers.title: Callback URL not approved
blockers.symptom: X returns error 415 'Callback URL not approved for this client application.' before the consent screen.
blockers.fix: Make the callback URL in the X app identical to the redirect URI in your Composio auth config, including any trailing slash. Copy it from the Composio dashboard, not from the older /api/v1/ path in Composio's Twitter guide.

blockers.title: Writes fail with 403 'Client Forbidden' or client-not-enrolled
blockers.symptom: Reads may work but posts fail; the body mentions registration_url and required_enrollment, or Composio reports client-not-enrolled or 'App not linked to project'.
blockers.fix: Attach the app to a project and enrol that project in pay-per-use billing in the console, then reconnect.

blockers.title: Requests blocked after the balance runs out
blockers.symptom: Every call fails once credits reach zero or the spending limit is hit.
blockers.fix: Add credits, raise the spending limit, or turn on auto-recharge with a recharge amount that outlasts a 5-minute burst.

blockers.title: Connection dies after 2 hours, or refresh fails with invalid_request
blockers.symptom: Tools start failing with auth errors shortly after connecting, or token refresh returns 'Value passed for the token was invalid'.
blockers.fix: Make sure offline.access is in the scopes in both the X app request and Composio, then reconnect. Developers report that X refresh tokens are single-use, so two processes refreshing the same token at once break the connection; let Composio be the only thing that refreshes it.

blockers.title: Replies, follows or likes fail while plain posts work
blockers.symptom: Reply posts are refused, and follow or like tools fail.
blockers.fix: These are X restrictions on self-serve access, not an auth problem. Replies only work when the original author mentioned or quoted the replying account; follows, likes and quote posts are off for self-serve. Re-authorizing does not help.

blockers.title: App-only tools return 401 while user tools work
blockers.symptom: Search, post lookup by IDs or usage tools fail with 401.
blockers.fix: Put the Bearer Token from the same X app as your OAuth Client ID into the Composio auth config. Adding user scopes does not fix it.

Create the app and copy its credentials (shown only once)
Verify a phone number, add a card and buy credits
